<!-- pr-reviewer: c9b8336f85afb8060b11af4eefc0a9f03b08ac08 -->
**Needs changes before merge** (one small item, the two-edge side rule).

**What looks good**
- Rotation math checks out: shortest arc with a safe antiparallel branch (half turn about the plane's first axis), edge pair as frame-to-frame R = T*S^T with d1 -> plane axis 1 and normal -> axis 3 (handedness consistent for G17/G18/G19), and a sine-based landing check (1e-9) that refuses a miss instead of storing a tilt.
- Document-frame datum is consistent: face normals, edge ends, the area-weighted centroid and `part_centre` are all read in the document frame (`model::transform_of` / `world_facets`), and picks are feature ids, so an already-aligned setup gives the same absolute answer (test `the_command_writes_..._alignment` pins the re-pick).
- Place-on-level math is right (anchor mapped through R and pos, only the plane-axis component removed; flip keeps the face at level 0).
- Work offset untouched (asserted); one undoable `AlignPartToSetup`, undo/redo pinned; 3-2-1 unchanged (`wcs_align` passes; `align.rs` only gains a pose parameter).
- No unwrap/expect/panic in new code, finite checks, new modules carry provenance, files well under 400 lines, `Fixes #330` and a `Changelog:` line present, decision file is per-issue.

**Local results (merged with current main; already up to date, no conflicts)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| app: plane_align / setup_align / pick / wcs_align / setups / setup_sheet / commands_undo / project_roundtrip / golden_cl | 9 / 9 / 9 / 5 / 11 / 7 / 32 / 68 / 23 passed, 0 failed |
| ui `--lib` (CWD crates/ui) | 294 passed, 2 ignored, 0 failed |
| clippy -D warnings, app and ui (all targets) | clean |

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/app/src/pick/plane.rs` `edge_datum` (the "plane's outside is the side away from the parts' centre" block): the side of a two-edge plane is guessed from the document bounds centre. That is wrong for concave/non-convex parts (e.g. two edges on a pocket floor or inner step of an L-bracket or thin plate, where the bbox centre lies on the outer side of that plane), and it silently lays the part upside down; when `dot(n, mid - centre)` is exactly or nearly 0 (plane through the centre) it silently keeps d1 x d2. Mis-orientation is gouge-class and the rule is to refuse by name. Please refuse when the offset is ambiguous (|dot| below a small tolerance, e.g. < 0.01 mm or a fraction of the part size) with a message such as "the two edges' plane runs through the middle of the part - pick a face, or use Flip", and/or use the facet winding of the faces adjacent to the edges to decide the side; at minimum add a test with a concave part and a plane-through-centre pair pinning whichever behaviour you choose.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- A re-pick that gives the identical alignment leaves Apply enabled and then refuses with "already holds the part that way" (also when the face already sits on the plane). Consider disabling Apply with that text, since `lay_on_plane` already knows the result.
- Not covered by tests: a zero-area/degenerate face refusal and a tilted-part antiparallel (`flip`) case; the code paths look right.
- Edge-pair picks are not shown with the resulting side before Apply; the viewport only shows it after (undoable).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 3516af14bcf27be62788b5b9f67f2f702c2a0f85 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (re-review of the delta c9b8336..3516af1; the one blocker is fixed).

**What looks good**
- The bbox-centre rule is gone. `edge_datum` (crates/app/src/pick/plane.rs:~219-232) now takes the outside from the one planar face both edges bound (`shared_face` / `bounded_faces`), read through the same `outward_normal` facet-winding reader as the single-face pick. The centre-plane ambiguity no longer exists.
- Refusals are by name: no common face, several, two bodies, or edge plane disagreeing with the face plane (`IN_FACE_SIN`) all refuse. The common-face case uses the exact text "the two edges do not bound one face, so their outside is not defined - pick the face instead". Skew edges are now refused; that is acceptable, since they span no plane and a guessed side is worse than a refusal.
- `AlignPartToSetup::check_lay` shares `change_of` with `new`, so Apply greys out on a repeat pick with the command's own message. `pick::plane_side` adds the "outside: +Z ..." line. No unwrap/expect/panic in the touched non-test code; files are all under 400 lines (plane.rs 336, setup_align.rs 267).
- New tests cover a concave L-bracket step with G17/G18/G19, both Flip values, upright and tilted, a plane through the centre, no common face, two bodies, a degenerate face, and an upside-down part. They assert the laid normal lands on the axis, and the concave fixture asserts the centre sits above the step, so it would have failed under the old rule.

**Local results (merged with current origin/main, no conflicts)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| build app + ui tests | ok |
| app plane_align | 9 passed |
| app plane_align_edges | 5 passed |
| app setup_align | 9 passed |
| app pick | 9 passed |
| app wcs_align | 5 passed |
| app commands_undo | 32 passed |
| app golden_cl | 23 passed |
| ui lib (CWD crates/ui) | 293 passed, 2 failed, 2 ignored |
| clippy -D warnings, app and ui | clean |

The 2 ui failures are `egui_shell_snapshot_light` and `tool_editor_snapshot` (pixel diffs). They fail identically on plain origin/main here, and the PR touches no snapshot, so they are not caused by this PR (most likely a platform/font artifact).

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Facet winding is trusted as the mesh's outside (align.rs `outward_normal`), with no check against the solid's signed volume. A mesh with globally inverted winding would lay the part upside down, silently. This is the same behaviour as the existing single-face pick and 3-2-1 alignment, so it is not new here. A cheap volume-sign check (refuse or warn when the signed volume is negative) would be a worthwhile follow-up issue covering all winding readers.
2. Skew edges are refused, as noted above; the message points the user to pick the face.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
